canonical: Angle P and Angle Q both turn through the same 1 hour-marks — an angle's size is the amount of turn between its arms, not how long the arms are drawn.

stem: Angle P is formed by two short arms that turn through 1 hour-marks on a clock face (like the hour hand sweeping from the 12 to the 1 mark). Angle Q is formed by two much longer arms that turn through the exact same 1 hour-marks. A student says Angle Q must be bigger because its arms are drawn longer. Based on the actual turn between the arms (not their length), how many hour-marks bigger is Angle Q than Angle P?
